title: Environment Setup for Linear, Regularized, and Logistic Regression
description: Import NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn regression/classification models, metrics, and datasets, then set the random seed and plot defaults.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `math`, `numpy`, `matplotlib.pyplot`, and scikit-learn tools for data splitting (`train_test_split`), preprocessing (`StandardScaler`, `PolynomialFeatures`), linear models (`LinearRegression`, `Ridge`, `Lasso`, `SGDRegressor`, `LogisticRegression`), and `Pipeline`.

Import regression and classification evaluation metrics (`mean_squared_error`, `r2_score`, `confusion_matrix`, `roc_curve`, `auc`, `classification_report`) and the built-in `load_breast_cancer` and `load_iris` datasets.
Set NumPy's random seed to the supplied value for reproducible runs, configure `plt.rcParams` for figure size `(6, 4)` and axes grid, and print `"Environment ready."`.

Notice the five linear models imported on line 10: `LinearRegression` (OLS), `Ridge` (L2 penalty), `Lasso` (L1 penalty), `SGDRegressor` (stochastic gradient descent), and `LogisticRegression` (classification).

steps.question: What does this setup cell print when executed?
steps.answer: It prints `Environment ready.` on line 23 after importing the libraries and configuring NumPy and Matplotlib.
